function: Over-the-air gradient aggregation across devices on a MIMO multiple-access channel: sparse-coded multiplexing with optimized precoding and post-processing; the learned model is a CNN classifier (pp. 7-13, 22).
system: MIMO multiple-access channel: PS with NR antennas, M=20 devices with NT antennas each (e.g., NT=8, NR=16), block fading, no RIS; band not stated (pp. 6, 23-24).
method: Gradient sparsification, partial-DFT compression, Turbo-CS recovery; precoders and post-processor by alternating optimization with ADMM (not learned); federated training of a small CNN with uploaded gradients (pp. 8-13, 19-22).
data_channel: Custom simulated i.i.d. Gaussian (Rayleigh) block fading with path loss, devices within 100 m of the PS; CNN trained on MNIST and Fashion-MNIST, i.i.d. and non-i.i.d. splits (pp. 22-23).
test_conditions: Training and testing use the same simulated channel model; antennas, streams, noise power are varied between experiments; no unseen scenario is tested (pp. 23-26).
baselines: Zero-forcing [16] and antenna selection [17] (channel inversion), AO-based beamforming [18] (single stream): earlier published MIMO over-the-air aggregation designs (pp. 3, 25).
metrics: Test accuracy versus round, channel uses needed to reach a relative target accuracy, compressed gradient aggregation MSE (pp. 23-27).
complexity: Order O(Imax(M N^3 log(1/eps) + N^3)) for the AO-ADMM design versus O(N^7 log(1/eps)) for the interior-point method (p. 21).
q1_support: p. 22: "i.i.d. drawn from CN (0, 1)"; the channel is a custom Rayleigh simulator with path loss, and the paper never uses a 3GPP model or measured data
q2_support: p. 23: "Fig. 6 demonstrates test accuracies versus the number of multiplexing streams"; each setting is a separate experiment and the paper never tests a trained model under a condition unseen in training
q3_support: p. 25: "zero-forcing [16], antennas selection [17], and AO-based beamforming [18]"; p. 26: "the SCoM approach consumes the least number of channel uses to achieve the same learning accuracy in all cases"
q4_support: p. 21: "the overall complexity of Algorithm 2 is given by"
q5_support: p. 23: "We train our network on two datasets: MNIST [33] and FMNIST [34]."; these are datasets of the learning task alone, no code or channel data link is given, and the channel is simulated (p. 22)
notes: PDF is the arXiv version (2304.04402v1) of the SCoM paper; it prints no DOI, so the DOI match rests on the title. The physical-layer design is classical (Turbo-CS, AO-ADMM); the work passes no_learning only through the over-the-air federated learning rule that the learned element is the model trained across the devices. q3 rests on the same rule: [18] is the earlier published aggregation design and [16], [17] are classical channel-inversion designs, compared on channel uses at equal accuracy.
